newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian stocks end up on resources support.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian stocks end up on resources support.

text.p: SPI futures 2396 +7 US 30yr cl 6.43 -0.02
10yrbond futs 92.850 -0.015 Gold (NY cl) 373.35 -.65
*Stocks ended firmer with resources underpinning gains after metal prices firmed. Volume 737.5 million shares, value A$1.39 bln, 1,096 stocks traded, 332 steady, 411 up, 353 down.
Australian shares finished higher on Thursday with gains underpinned by a stronger resource sector which was buoyed by firmer metal prices and takeover activity in the gold sector.

The key share market barometer, the All Ordinaries index, closed 9.6 points firmer at 2,386.3. The December share price index futures contract closed seven points up at 2,396 and at a 9.7 point premium to the underlying index.
Turnover was lifted by a heavy activity in the gold sector following bids for Papua New Guinea gold miner Highlands Gold and Placer Pacific by Canada's Placer Dome Inc.

"There was a buying frenzy in gold stocks spurred by the takeover offers and the excitement surrounding discoveries in the Gawler Craton. This was definitely the driving force behind the market's gains today," said Joseph Pagliaro, client advisor at Brisbane broker Wilson HTM.
Pagliaro said the substantial interest in the gold sector rubbed off on other resource sectors as investor optimism rose.
"I think it will settle down tommorrow but the price of gold is due for a bounce," he said.
Dealers said trade was likely to be quiet on Friday due to the closure of U.S. markets for the Thanksgiving day holiday.

Canadian gold group Placer Dome Inc's bid for Papua New Guinea gold miners Highlands Gold and the remaining 25 percent of Placer Pacific caused a rush on the stock of other PNG gold stocks with Goldfields and Lihir Gold bid much higher.
The gold sector was the outstanding market segment on the day while big resource stocks BHP and CRA underpinned the market's gains after the price of copper continued to recover.

Brisbane-based pastoral company Primac was one of the most active stocks with fellow pastoral group Elders buying a strategic 17 percent stake following a hostile takeover offer for Primac from Perth-based IAMA in September.

In other markets, Australian bond yields ended little changed after a fairly thinly traded, range bound session as the market waited for a speech from the governor of the Reserve Bank in Melbourne later today.
The yield on 10-year T-bonds ended at 7.15 percent, up 0.01 percentage point from Wednesday's close.
The Australian dollar was relaxed around the 81 U.S. cent level in late local trade with option-related offers at US$0.8130 seen impeding an uptrend.
At 4.50 p.m. (0550 GMT), the local currency was quoted at US$0.8095/00.

FUTURES/OPTIONS - Options activity was lifted to even higher levels by heavy trade in the resources sector stimulated by the takeover activity in the gold sector. Futures were quieter ahead of the U.S. holiday.
